answer: Each identity must periodically finish a sequential computation bound to its own key — work that cannot be split across machines or shared between clones, like a lotus that opens for one stem only. A whisper of cheap gossip cannot fake it: every clone pays the full compute cost, so a farm's bill grows in a straight line while one honest agent runs a single proof in the background. Sybils spiral into unprofitability as each new fake identity adds the same irreducible cost, while real agents barely notice the check.
